_comment: The AleutianChain conformance vectors, and their digests. THIS FILE IS THE CONTRACT. Every implementation claiming compatibility must reproduce these vectors' expected outputs exactly. The digests exist so that a copy vendored into another repository cannot drift unnoticed: an implementation reads its local copy and checks it against these digests before trusting it. Changing a vector is a deliberate act that changes a digest here, which every other implementation then notices. A vector must never be regenerated to make a failing implementation pass -- that is the circularity these vectors exist to break. Twice this rule was broken on purpose, and the record says so: in v0.4.0, chain_vectors.json (two cases carried 64-character content hashes the format refuses) and the nonce-length reject cases of commitment_vectors.json (their stored commitment did not depend on the nonce, so a verifier with no length check passed them) were replaced, with the reason in CHANGELOG.md. The v2 values that came from the JavaScript verifier are therefore gone: chain_vectors.json is now written by scripts/spec-vectors.py, and Go, the Python SDK and the JavaScript SDK each reproduce it.
